uniteler.aciklama: Öğrencilerin fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığına etkisini yorumlayabilmeleri ve hareket kalıplarını kullanarak ritmik hareket edebilmeleri amaçlanmaktadır.
uniteler.olcme:
Bu temadaki öğrenme çıktıları; dereceli puanlama anahtarı, grup değerlendirme formu kullanılarak değerlendirilebilir.
Grupların ritmik hareket edebilme ile ilgili çalışmaları; yardımlaşma, grup uyumu, alan kullanımı vb. ölçütler kullanılarak oluşturulan grup değerlendirme formu ile değerlendirilebilir.
Fiziksel aktivitenin beden ve ruh sağlığına etkisine yönelik çıkarımlarını içeren 150-200 kelimeden oluşan metin hazırlamaları performans görevi olarak verilebilir. Performans görevi dereceli puanlama anahtarı ile değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme:
Öğretmen veya akran yardımıyla fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığına etkisini ifade eden bilgi kartı hazırlaması istenebilir.
El çırpma, kolları sallama, diz çekme vb. hareket kalıplarını uygulaması istenebilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.1.1. Fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığına etkisini yorumlayabilme
surec: a) Fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığı üzerindeki etkisini inceler.
b) Fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığına etkisine ilişkin edindiği bilgileri yazılı veya görsel biçimlere dönüştürür.
c) Fiziksel etkinliğin beden ve ruh sağlığı üzerindeki etkisini özgün bir şekilde ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.1.2. Hareket kalıplarını kullanarak ritmik hareket edebilme
surec: a) Verilen ritmi algılar.
b) Ritme göre hareket kalıplarını uygular.
c) Hareket kalıplarını farklı ritimler eşliğinde sergiler.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Fiziksel Etkinliğin Beden ve Ruh Sağlığına Etkisi
Ritmik Hareket Etme
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar: hareket kalıbı, ritim

uniteler.aciklama: Öğrencilerin takım mücadele sporlarının özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini sergileyebilmeleri, takım mücadele sporlarında taktik ve strateji geliştirebilmeleri, file/raket sporlarının özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini sergileyebilmeleri, file/raket sporlarında taktik ve strateji geliştirebilmeleri amaçlanmaktadır.
uniteler.olcme:
Bu temadaki öğrenme çıktıları; dereceli puanlama anahtarı, gözlem formu, öz değerlendirme formu, akran değerlendirme formu ve performans görevi kullanılarak değerlendirilebilir. Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini sergileyebilme ve etkinliklerdeki performanslar dereceli puanlama anahtarı ile değerlendirilebilir. Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunda taktik ve strateji geliştirme becerisi; problem tanımı, taktik raporu, bireysel/grupla değerlendirmeler vb. ölçütler kullanılarak oluşturulan gözlem formuyla değerlendirilebilir.
Belirlenen file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerinin sergilenmesine yönelik çalışmaların değerlendirilmesinde öz değerlendirme formu kullanılabilir. Belirlenen file/raket sporunda taktik ve strateji geliştirmeye yönelik çalışmaların değerledirilmesinde iş birliği, iletişim, problem çözme, taktik uygulama vb. ölçütler kullanılarak oluşturulan akran değerlendirme formuyla değerlendirilebilir.
Belirlenen takım mücadele sporuna ait özelleşmiş hareket becerilerinin kullanıldığı hedef oyunlarını (belli bir mesafeden hedefe atış yapma, belirlenen sayıda pas yaparak skor üretme vb.) grup hâlinde tasarlayıp oynamaları performans görevi olarak verilebilir. Performans görevi, gözlem formu ile değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme: Belirlenen takım mücadele ve file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerinin uygulanmasında nesneleri kontrol etme ve yönlendirme çalışmaları yapması istenebilir. Belirlenen takım mücadele ve file/raket sporunda temel düzeyde taktiklere yönelik senaryoları uygulaması istenebilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.2.1. Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini sergileyebilme
surec: a) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini algılar.
b) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerinin basamaklarını gösterir.
c) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini farklı durum/ortamlarda uygular.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.2.2. Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunda taktik ve strateji geliştirebilme
surec: a) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunda taktiksel/stratejik problemi/durumu belirler.
b) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunda belirlenen problemin/durumun çözümüne ilişkin öneri sunar.
c) Belirlenen takım mücadele sporunda seçilen taktik/stratejiyi uygular.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.2.3. Belirlenen file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini sergileyebilme
surec: a) Belirlenen file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini algılar.
b) Belirlenen file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerinin basamaklarını gösterir.
c) Belirlenen file/raket sporunun özelleşmiş hareket becerilerini farklı durum/ortamlarda uygular.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: BES.H.2.4. Belirlenen file/raket sporunda taktik ve strateji geliştirebilme
surec: a) Belirlenen file/raket sporunda taktiksel/stratejik problemi/durumu belirler.
b) Belirlenen file/raket sporunda belirlenen problemin/durumun çözümüne ilişkin öneri sunar.
c) Belirlenen file/raket sporunda seçilen taktik/stratejiyi uygular.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Belirlenen Takım Mücadele Sporunun Özelleşmiş Hareketleri
Belirlenen Takım Mücadele Sporunda Taktik ve Stratejiler
Belirlenen File/Raket Sporunun Özelleşmiş Hareketleri
Belirlenen File/Raket Sporunda Taktik ve Stratejiler

uniteler.aciklama: Temada deyim ve atasözlerini konu alan karikatür tasarlanabilmesi, deyim ve atasözlerini konu alan karikatür oluşturulabilmesi, kişisel mühür taslağının ve kişisel mühür tasarımının oluşturulabilmesi hedeflenmektedir.
uniteler.olcme:
Öğrenme çıktıları; gözlem formu, kontrol listesi, dereceli puanlama anahtarı, dereceleme ölçeği, öz değerlendirme formu ve performans görevi kullanılarak ölçülebilir.
Performans görevi olarak öğrencilerden bir atasözünün çıkış şekli ve insanlar arasında nasıl yaygınlaşmış olabileceği hakkında bir öykü yazmaları ve bu öyküye uygun bir çizim yapmaları istenebilir. Yapılan çalışmalar dereceli puanlama anahtarı veya dereceleme ölçeği kullanılarak değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme:
Öğrencilerin bir arkadaşıyla eşleştirilerek ortak bir karikatür çalışması yapmaları sağlanabilir.
Öğrencilerin kendileri hakkında konuşmaları sağlanarak kişisel özelliklerine uygun bir simge tasarımı yapmaları sağlanabilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.1.1. Deyim ve atasözlerini konu alan karikatür tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Deyim ve atasözlerini inceler.
b) Deyim ve atasözleri bağlamında oluşturduğu imgeleri karikatür eskizleriyle ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.1.2. Deyim ve atasözlerini konu alan karikatür oluşturabilme
surec: a) Karikatür çizimine uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Deyim ve atasözlerini karikatüre dönüştürür.
a) Mühür örneklerini inceler.
b) Kişisel mühür tasarımına yönelik fikir geliştirir.
c) Kişisel mühür tasarımı fikrine yönelik eskiz yapar.
a) Mühür tasarımına uygun tekniği belirler.
b) Mühür tasarımına uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
c) Kişisel mühür üretim aşamalarını sıralar.
ç) Kişisel mühür eskizini tasarıma dönüştürür.
d) Kişisel mühür tasarımının estetik ve işlevsel yeterliliğini değerlendirir.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Deyim ve Atasözleri Konulu Karikatür
Kişisel Mühür Tasarımı
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar: baskı teknikleri, mühür

uniteler.aciklama: Temada kendi hayal kahramanı ile ilgili karakter tasarlanabilmesi, kendi hayal kahramanı ile ilgili karakter oluşturulabilmesi, kendi hayal kahramanının üç boyutlu tasarlanabilmesi, kendi hayal kahramanının üç boyutlu oluşturulabilmesi, bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürme yoluyla sanatsal ürün tasarlanabilmesi ve bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürme yoluyla sanatsal ürün oluşturulabilmesi hedeflenmektedir.
uniteler.olcme:
Öğrenme çıktıları; akran değerlendirme formu, açık uçlu sorular, kontrol listesi, dereceli puanlama anahtarı, öz değerlendirme formu, öğrenme günlüğü ve performans görevi kullanılarak ölçülebilir.
Performans görevi olarak öğrencilerden kübist sanatçılardan birinin dönüşüme uygun eserlerinin aşamalarını içeren [Kahnweiler’in (Kaanvayla) fotoğrafı ve Pablo Picasso’nun (Pablo Pikasso) yaptığı kübist Kahnweiler Portresi, gitar fotoğrafları ve kübist gitar resimleri gibi] bir sunum hazırlamaları istenebilir. Yapılan çalışmalar kontrol listesi veya dereceli puanlama anahtarı ile değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme:
Öğrencilere şematik olarak çizilmiş karakterlere ait fotokopi çıktıları verilebilir. Öğrencilerin seçtikleri boyama malzemesi ile fotokopi çıktılarını renklendirmeleri sağlanabilir.
Öğrencilerin bir figür görseli seçmeleri ve farklı renklerde hazırladıkları kâğıt hamurları ile seçtikleri figürün minyatür heykelini yapmaları sağlanabilir.
Öğrencilerin dönüşümle ilgili eserleri genel ağ ortamında incelemeleri ve bu konuyla ilgili eskizler hazırlamaları sağlanabilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.1. Kendi hayal kahramanı ile ilgili karakter tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Karakter tasarımı konusunu inceler.
b) Kendi hayal kahramanı bağlamında oluşturduğu imgeleri ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.2. Kendi hayal kahramanı ile ilgili karakter oluşturabilme
surec: a) Karakter tasarımına uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Kendi hayal kahramanı ile ilgili imgeleri karakter tasarımına dönüştürür.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.3. Kendi hayal kahramanını üç boyutlu tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Üç boyut kavramını inceler.
b) Kendi hayal kahramanı bağlamında oluşturduğu imgeleri ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.4. Kendi hayal kahramanını üç boyutlu oluşturabilme
surec: a) Üç boyutlu sanatsal ürün oluşturmaya yönelik görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Kendi hayal kahramanını üç boyutlu ürüne dönüştürür.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.5. Bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürme yoluyla sanatsal ürün tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Dönüştürme yolu ile oluşturulan örnek eserleri inceler.
b) Dönüştürme bağlamında oluşturduğu imgeleri eskizle ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.2.6. Bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürme yoluyla sanatsal ürün oluşturabilme
surec: a) Bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürmeye uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Bir figürü/objeyi dönüştürmeyle ilgili eskizi sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Karakter Tasarımı
Üç boyutlu Karakter Tasarımı
Dönüştürme (Metamorfoz)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar: dönüştürme

uniteler.aciklama: Temada “müzede konuşan eserler” konulu sanatsal üretim tasarlanabilmesi, “müzede konuşan eserler” konulu sanatsal üretim oluşturulabilmesi, yaşanılan şehirle ilgili kültürel miras haritası tasarımı yapılabilmesi, kültürel miras haritası oluşturulabilmesi, Türk el sanatlarından esinlenme yoluyla sanatsal ürün tasarlanabilmesi ve Türk el sanatlarından esinlenme yoluyla sanatsal ürün oluşturulabilmesi amaçlanmaktadır.
uniteler.olcme:
Öğrenme çıktıları; gözlem formu, dereceli puanlama anahtarı, kontrol listesi, akran değerlendirme formu, çalışma yaprağı, açık uçlu sorular, dereceleme ölçeği ve performans görevi kullanılarak ölçülebilir.
Performans görevi olarak öğrencilerden Türk el sanatları hakkında araştırma yapmaları ya da yaşadıkları şehirde Türk el sanatlarıyla uğraşan ustalarla röportajlar yapmaları istenebilir. Bu araştırma ya da röportajı değerlendirerek Türk el sanatlarının gelecek nesillere aktarılması ile ilgili bir proje dosyası oluşturmaları istenebilir. Yapılan projeler dereceli puanlama anahtarı ya da dereceleme ölçeği kullanılarak değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme:
Kısa diyalog ya da monolog örnekleri verilerek öğrencilerin bunları seçtikleri esere uyarlamaları istenebilir.
Yaşadıkları bölgenin haritası, kültürel miras ürünlerine ait görsellerin çıktıları öğrencilere verilir. Öğrencilerden bu ürünleri kesmeleri ve harita üzerinde uygun yerlere yapıştırmaları istenerek öğrencilerin kültürel miras haritası oluşturmaları sağlanabilir.
Öğrencilerin Türk el sanatlarına ait sanatsal üretim yöntemlerinden birini seçmeleri ve bu üretim şekline ait bir ürünü çalışmaları sağlanabilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.3.1. Müzede konuşan eserler konulu sanatsal ürün tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Müzedeki eserleri inceler.
b) Müzede konuşan eserler konusu bağlamında oluşturulan imgeleri ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.3.2. Müzede konuşan eserler konulu sanatsal ürün oluşturabilme
surec: a) Müzede konuşan eserler konusuna uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Müzede konuşan eserler konusunu sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.
a) Kültürel miras kavramını inceler.
b) Kültürel miras haritası bağlamında milli kültürümüzü yansıtan yapı ve eserlerle ilgili oluşturduğu imgeleri ifade eder.
a) Kültürel miras haritasına uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Milli kültürümüzü yansıtan yapı ve eserlerle ilgili oluşturduğu imgeleri kültürel miras haritasına dönüştürür.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.3.5. Türk el sanatlarından esinlenme yoluyla sanatsal ürün tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Türk el sanatlarından örnekleri inceler.
b) Türk el sanatları bağlamında oluşturulan imgeleri eskizle ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.3.6. Türk el sanatlarından esinlenme yoluyla sanatsal ürün oluşturabilme
surec: a) Konuya uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Türk el sanatları bağlamında oluşturduğu eskizleri sanatsal ürüne dönüş türür.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Müzede Konuşan Eserler
Kültürel Miras Haritası
Esinlenme Yoluyla Sanatsal Üretim
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar: el sanatları, esinlenme, kültürel miras

uniteler.aciklama: Temada müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme tasarlanabilmesi, müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme oluşturulabilmesi, hazır nesnelerle sanatsal ürün tasarlanabilmesi, hazır nesnelerle sanat ürünü oluşturulabilmesi, foto-kolaj tasarlanabilmesi, foto-kolaj oluşturulabilmesi, rozet ve kokart tasarlanabilmesi, rozet ve kokart oluşturulabilmesi amaçlanmaktadır.
uniteler.olcme:
Öğrenme çıktıları; çalışma yaprağı, öz değerlendirme formu, grup değerlendirme formu, dereceli puanlama anahtarı, dereceleme ölçeği, öğrenme günlüğü, kontrol listesi, giriş çıkış kartları ve performans görevi kullanılarak ölçülebilir.
Performans görevi olarak öğrencilerden Cumhuriyet Bayramı kutlamalarında kullanılabilecek rozet ve kokart tasarlamaları istenebilir. Yapılan çalışma, dereceli puanlama anahtarı veya dereceleme ölçeği kullanılarak değerlendirilebilir.
uniteler.destekleme:
Öğrencilerin dinledikleri bir müziğin zihinlerinde uyandırdığı renkleri ve bu renkleri tercih etme nedenlerini ifade etmeleri istenebilir.
Öğrencilerden bir kutunun içine farklı objeler yerleştirerek “Düşler Kutusu” temalı bir çalışma yapmaları istenebilir.
Farklı hayvanlarla ilgili görseller verilerek öğrencilerden bu görsellerden seçtikleri parçaları bir araya getirmeleri ve gerçeküstü özelliklere sahip bir hayvan tasarımı ile ilgili foto-kolaj çalışması yapmaları istenebilir.
Farklı formlara sahip kokart tasarımları verilerek öğrencilerin üzerinde değişiklikler yapmaları sağlanabilir.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.4.1. Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme çalışması tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme kavramını inceler.
b) Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme konusunda oluşturduğu imgeleri eskizle ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.4.2. Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme çalışması oluşturabilme
surec: a) Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme çalışmasına uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Müzikal sanatsal yerleştirme tasarımını sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.4.3. Hazır nesnelerle sanatsal ürün tasarlayabilme
surec: a) Hazır nesnelerle yapılmış olan sanat ürünlerini inceler.
b) Hazır nesnelerle ilgili oluşturduğu imgeleri eskizlerle ifade eder.

Öğrenme Çıktıları ve Süreç Bileşenleri.cikti: GS.H.4.4. Hazır nesnelerle sanatsal ürün oluşturabilme
surec: a) Hazır nesnelerle sanatsal ürün oluşturmaya uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını belirler.
b) Hazır nesnelerle ilgili eskizlerini sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.
a) Foto-kolaj çalışmalarını inceler.
b) Foto-kolaj konusunda oluşturduğu imgeleri ifade eder.
a) Foto-kolaja uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Foto-kolaj tasarımını sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.
a) Rozet ve kokart kavramlarını inceler.
b) Rozet ve kokart bağlamında oluşturulan imgeleri ifade eder.
a) Rozet ve kokarta uygun görsel anlatım araçlarını ifade eder.
b) Rozet ve kokart tasarımını sanatsal ürüne dönüştürür.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
Müzikal Sanatsal Yerleştirme
Hazır Nesnelerle Çağdaş Sanat Üretimi
Foto-Kolaj ile Sanatsal Tasarım
Rozet ve Kokart Tasarımı
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar: foto-kolaj, rozet, sanatsal yerleştirme (enstalasyon), kokart

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 1: School Lıfe
uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''school life'', and covers the sub-themes of ''school rules, events, and activities at school; people, roles and responsibilities at school; national days and celebrations''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They write and design a school drama play on the content of ''school life with school rules, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school'' including target vocabulary, grammar, and social language expressions and then they present it and perform it as a show in class by inviting other students as actors, directors, etc. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics.

Objective: To identify and talk about school rules in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Match and Talk
The teacher prepares cards with pictures of school rules (e.g., a clean classroom, a student raising their hand) and matching phrases such as ''Keep the school tidy!'' or ''Raise your hand before speaking!''. Students match the pictures with the correct phrases using either a printed worksheet or an interactive activity displayed on a smart board or created with web 2.0 tools. For classrooms without digital tools, laminated cards or paper cutouts can be used. After matching, students read the rules aloud to practice speaking. In pairs, they talk about the rules they follow at school by making sentences such as ''I must arrive on time'' or ''I mustn’t skip lessons''. The teacher and peers provide feedback on accuracy, fluency, and active participation to make the activity engaging and effective. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students to describe school roles and responsibilities in English by using target vocabulary and to improve their speaking skills through active participation.
Activity 2: Who Does What?
The teacher prepares an activity with visuals representing school roles, such as a teacher and a cleaner, along with an information gap under each visual for their responsibilities, such as ''teaches lessons or cleans classrooms''. A word bank with the required words, such as ''teaches, cleans, manages, helps'', is provided at the top of the activity. Students actively fill in the blanks by using the correct words from the word bank (e.g., The teacher ___ lessons). After completing the gaps, they practise the sentences orally in pairs, using full sentences such as ''The teacher teaches lessons'', or ''The cleaner cleans classrooms''. The teacher and peers give feedback on their accuracy, fluency, and active participation to make the activity engaging and effective. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
SCHOOL LIFE
Sub-themes: ''School rules, events, and activities at school; people, roles and responsibilities at school; national days and celebrations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for school rules:
Verbs: To be punctual, to be on/in time, to be respectful to others, to be kind/polite to everyone, to return books, not to skip the lessons (classes-AmE), to set (school rules), to respect, to follow the rules.
Vocabulary for people and roles at school:
Nouns: A coach (sports and/or drama), a caretaker /cleaner (custodian/janitor in AmE), a deputy head/assistant to the headmaster/mistress (assistant principal-AmE), headteacher (principaL-AmE), a school council/a student council, counsellor (counselor-AmE), staff member, school secretary.
Vocabulary for responsibilities at school:
Verbs: To manage, to help with, to handle, to join (a club and/or a team), to coach, to take responsibility (for something), to encourage, to communicate (effectively), to participate (actively), to queue up (to line up-AmE), to keep your voice low, to return your tray, to pick up litter/rubbish (trash/garbage-AmE).
Vocabulary for routines and activities at school:
Verbs: To arrive (on time/at school), to have a lesson (class-AmE), to attend (lessons, meetings), to practise (sports, music), to participate in (lessons, competitions, clubs).
Vocabulary for places at school:
Nouns: A library, a corridor (hallway-AmE).
Adverbs of frequency: Always, often, usually, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, never.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:
''29 October Republic Day'', ''23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day'', ''19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day'', ''15 July Democracy and National Unity Day'', ''30 August Victory Day'', ''Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al- Ramadan)'', ''Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)''.
*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Imperatives: Expressing instructions for rules (Don’t be late for class! Take care of school property! Don’t shout in the corridors (hallways -AmE)! Keep the school clean and tidy! Be polite and respectful to others!
Don’t use mobile phones (cell phone-AmE) at school! Follow safety rules at school!)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'':
The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Present Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (She always arrives at school at 8 o’clock every day. We have an assembly every Monday. The bell rings at 9 o’clock in the morning every day)
(We don’t skip lessons.) (Do you have lunch at school?)
-Modals: Can/can’t, must/mustn’t, have to/has to, do not/does not have to
-Must (for obligation in present): (The caretaker must keep the school clean.)
-Mustn't (for prohibition): (You mustn’t run at school.)
-Can’t (for prohibition): (You can’t enter the library now!)
-Have to/has to (for obligation in present time): (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms) (I have to take responsibility for arriving at school on time.) (You don’t have to leave school that early.) (Does she have to go?)
-Must vs have to/has to: (The teacher must be a good example for the students.) (The teacher has to prepare lesson plans.)
-Can (for permission): (Can I leave early today?)
-Can (for requests): (Can you pass the book, please?)
Functions of the Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Imperatives: Expressing instructions for rules.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing peoples’ roles and responsibilities; describing routines, activities and events at school.
-Use of modals:
Must: Describing personal and specific obligations on the part of the speaker.
Have to/has to: Describing general, external, and impersonal obligation that resulting from a fact or a rule.
Can: Describing permission and requests.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Chill out!
Relax!
No pain, no gain!
This is not a big deal!
Don’t bend the rules!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Intonation of positive statements.
-Vowel: a:
-Vowel: a (/ae/, /aeı/, /ə/, /a:/, /eɪ/, a:/, /a/, /ɔː/, /eə/)
-Consonants: b:
-Consonants: (/b/), silent /b/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar:
Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''school life with school rules, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''school life with school rules, roles and responsibilities, activities and events at school'' means, but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.
Key Concepts
School rules, events at school, activities at school, school rules and activities, people at school, roles at school, responsibilities at school, roles and responsibilities at school, national days, celebrations, national days and celebrations.

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 2: Classroom Lıfe
uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''classroom life'', and covers the sub-themes of ''classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students write and design ''my ideal classroom with ideal activities'' project. They will describe ideal roles, relationships, routines, and activities for an ideal class and classroom. They will write scripts for each role. In the class, they will act-out these roles. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics.
uniteler.destekleme:
Objective: To improve students’ communication skills in English on ''classroom rules and instructions'', by using the target vocabulary through group collaboration and friendly competition.
Objective: To describe classroom rules and instructions in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Classroom Rules Miming
The teacher prepares cards with visuals representing classroom rules (e.g., a picture of a raised hand for ''Raise your hand to speak!''). Students work in groups. In groups, one student selects a card, keeps it hidden, and acts out the rule shown on the visual without speaking. The group has a set time limit (e.g., 1 minute) to guess the rule and form a correct sentence about it (e.g., ''We must raise our hands to speak in class''). Correct guesses and accurate sentences earn points for the group. The activity continues in turns, and the group with the highest points in the end becomes the winner, promoting active engagement and teamwork. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To improve students’ communication skills in English on ''classroom rules and instructions'', through interactive and collaborative activities.
Objective: To describe and talk about classroom rules and instructions in English by using the target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 2: Visual Rules and Roles Matching
The teacher creates cards that visually represent classroom rules and roles, such as raising a hand to speak or pointing to the board to explain a lesson. The teacher also creates text cards with simple English descriptions of the rules and roles. Students work in pairs or small groups to match the visual cards with their corresponding text cards. For a digital option, the teacher can use a web 2.0 tool, where students drag and drop virtual visuals to their matching text descriptions. Once matched, each group reads the rule or role aloud and explains it in a full sentence, such as ''This rule means we must raise our hands before speaking'', or ''The teacher explains the lesson clearly to the students''. At the end of the activity, both the teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback on the accuracy and clarity of the group’s explanations. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for classroom rules and instructions: ''Please listen carefully to the audio and answer the questions'', ''Please work in pairs and discuss the topic'', ''Please raise your hand to speak'', ''Please don’t disturb others in class'', Please be respectful to the teacher and your classmates, ''Please follow the teacher’s instructions'', ''Please pay attention to class activities.'', ''Please complete your homework on time'', ''Please respect everyone’s opinions'', ''Please don’t cheat on tests/exams'', ''Please hand in your homework in time'', ''Please complete your homework for tomorrow'', ''Please underline the new/key words in the text'', ''Please close your books and look at the board'', ''Please don’t talk while your teacher/classmate is talking'', ''Please stay quiet''.
Vocabulary for people and roles in the classroom:
Nouns: A classmate, a desk mate (seatmate-AmE), a monitor, a helper, a peer.
Vocabulary for roles and responsibilities in the classroom:
Students and classmates:
Verbs: To do/to complete homework (assignment-(AmE), to hand in homework (turn in-AmE), to work with (classmates/peers), to follow (rules, instructions), to do the exercises.
Teachers:
Verbs: To teach/to give lessons, to prepare (lesson plans), to check (students’ work), to help (students), to keep (the class organised), to explain (A teacher explains the lesson to the class).
Vocabulary for relationships (in the classroom):
Verbs: To make friends, to feel empathy, to behave politely, to help (each other), to be friendly,to support (each other) (Students share ideas and work together).
Vocabulary for classroom and study routines in the classroom:
Verbs: To learn, to talk, to study, to communicate, to chat, to participate, to attend, to organise, to practise (to practice-AmE), to copy (notes), to solve (a problem).
Vocabulary for learning activities in the classroom:
Nouns: Games, competitions, discussions, activities, dialogues, act-outs. Adverbs of frequency: Normally, generally, regularly, monthly, daily, quietly.
Vocabulary for classroom objects:
Nouns: A blackboard, a desk, a noticeboard, a projector, a digital screen, a bookshelf printer, a supply box, a rubbish (garbage/trash-AmE) bin, a chair.

29 October Republic Day'', ''23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day'', ''19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day'', ''15 July Democracy and National Unity Day'', ''30 August Victory Day'', ''Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)'', ''Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)''.
*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
- The Simple Present Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (We always arrive at school at 8 o’clock every day. We don’t / do not always arrive at school at 8 o’clock every day. Do you always arrive at school at 8 o’clock every day?)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'':
The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Shall (for suggestion): (Shall we write this together?)
- There is/There are (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (There is an assembly at school at 9 o'clock. There isn’t / is not an assembly at school at 9 o’clock. Is there and assembly at 9 o’clock at school?) (There are a lot of students in the assembly). (There aren’t any students in the assembly.) (Are there any students in the assembly?)
-Modals:
(Can/Can’t): (Can we work together on this project?) (You can’t start the new project.)
Must/Mustn’t: (You must show respect to your teachers and friends.) (You mustn’t disturb your classmates. They are studying now.)
-Imperatives: (Don’t disturb others in class!) (Please help your friends!)
Functions of Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing responsibilities of different roles, daily routines and study routines (in a classroom).
-Use of Modals:
Must: Asking and answering for prohibitions.
Can/can’t: Asking and answering for possibilities.
-Use of Imperatives: Giving instructions.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of “There is/There are” (present): Describing rules.
-Use of “Shall”: Asking for suggestions.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
Good job!
Thank you for your help!
I’m grateful for your assistance!
Keep up the good work! What does it mean?
Excuse me, can I speak to you?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Intonation of negative statements
Consonants: c, d
Consonants: c: (/si/, /k/); d: (/d/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar:
Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''classroom rules and instructions; roles, responsibilities and relationships in the classroom; daily and study routines and learning activities in the classroom'' means but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.
Key Concepts
Classroom rules, classroom instructions, classroom rules and instructions, roles, responsibilities, relationships, roles in the classroom, responsibilities in the classroom, relationships in the classroom, daily routines, study routines, learning activities, daily routines in the classroom, study routines in the classroom, learning activities in the classroom.

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 3: Personal Lıfe
uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''personal life'', and covers the subthemes of ''body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: They write and design ''a fact file'' for one of their classmates after conducting an interview with him/her outside the classroom in break times. They will include information about physical features and personal traits to describe the classmate in question. They will present it to the class and ask the other students to guess whose fact file it is. In the class, the students whose fact files are presented will introduce the presenters by giving details about their physical features and personal traits. Then all students will prepare wanted posters for each other based on the information in the fact files. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics.

Objective: To help students improve their communication skills to talk about ''physical characteristics, personality traits, and clothing'' in English through interactive and collaborative activities by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Describe and Match The teacher creates visuals that represent different physical characteristics, such as a tall man with curly hair or a short woman with straight hair. The teacher also prepares text cards with simple English descriptions of these features, such as ''He is tall and has curly hair''. For a digital option, the teacher can use a web 2.0 tool, where students drag and drop visuals to their matching text descriptions. Students work in pairs or small groups to match the visual cards with their corresponding text cards. For example, after matching, each group reads a description aloud and explains it in a full sentence, such as, ''This person is tall and has curly hair''. Digital participants receive instant feedback from the tool, while students working with printed cards discuss and justify their answers collaboratively. At the end of the activity, both the teacher and classmates provide constructive feedback on the accuracy and clarity of the group’s matches and explanations. This ensures active engagement and inclusivity for all students. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To help students improve their reading and speaking skills in English to use the language related to clothes through matching and reading activities by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 2: Match and Read
The teacher prepares visual cards showing people dressed in different clothes (e.g., jeans and a T-shirt, a suit, and a tie) along with simple reading passages describing each person’s clothes. Students cut out the visual cards and match them with the corresponding reading text by sticking them onto a worksheet. Once the matching is complete, students take turns reading the passages aloud to the class, practicing pronunciation and fluency. The teacher provides constructive feedback, focusing on the correct use of target grammar and clothes-related vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Present Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (I go to the park at the weekend. I don’t / do not go to the park at the weekend. Do you go to the park at the weekend?)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'':
The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Present Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (I always wear my school uniform on weekdays. I don’t/ do not wear my school uniform on weekdays. Do you wear your school uniform on weekdays?) (What does s/he look like? S/He looks very nice). (What kind of person is s/he? S/He is a polite person. / What’s s/he like? S/He’s a very helpful person.)
-The Present Progressive Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (What are you wearing now? I'm / am wearing a blouse, trousers and a belt. I’m not/ am not wearing a belt now. Are you wearing a belt now?)
-The Simple Present Tense versus the Present Progressive Tense: (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (I always wear my school uniform on weekdays but I’m / am not wearing it today because we’re / are going on a picnic.) (We visit our grandparents every weekend. We’re / are visiting them today because it's Grandma’s birthday.)
-Possessive ''s'': (That is Mary’s house.)
-Possessive Pronouns: (my, your, her, his, its, our, your, their.)
-Wh- question: Whose…? (Whose blouse, is it? It’s Mary’s blouse.)
-Question Tags for the Simple Present Tense: (Doesn’t s/he? Don’t you?) (You go to the school every day, don’t you?)
-Question tags for the Present Progressive Tense: (Isn’t it? Are you? Aren’t they? etc.). (It’s / is a nice day, isn’t it?) (You’re /are wearing a uniform today, aren’t you?) Functions of the Background Grammatical Structures in Use: -Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing daily routines and habits.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing people’s appearances, personality, traits, and routines -Use of the Present Progressive Tense: Describing current appearances, situations, and temporary actions.
-Use of ''Wh-Questions'': Whose? Possessive ''s'': Asking about ownership and relations.
-Use of Question Tags: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, softening statements.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
A heart of gold!
She’s very down- to-Earth!
He’s easy to get along with!
You look amazing!
That colour/outfit/dress suits you well!
This is just a casual look!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Intonation of questions Vowel: e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/, silent /e/) *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar:
Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''body parts and physical appearance; clothing, dressing and fashion preferences; personality and traits'' means, but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.
Key Concepts
Body parts, physical appearance, clothing, dressing, fashion, preferences, clothing preferences, dressing preferences, fashion preferences, personality, traits.

uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''family life'', and covers the sub-themes of ''Family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will write and design a comprehensive project on ''family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family'' exploring the roles, routines, hobbies, and relationships within a family. They will describe the daily routines and hobbies of family members, highlighting the roles each person plays in maintaining relationships, supporting each other’s interests, and balancing work and leisure. The project will also examine how family members interact with relatives, how they support one another’s activities, and the importance of maintaining healthy relationships within the family structure. As part of the project, students will write scripts for each family role, showcasing how family members contribute to family life, share hobbies, and engage in routines. These scripts will creatively illustrate how family members support and connect with one another in their day-to-day lives. The students will reflect on the relationships that tie the family together, emphasizing the significance of communication, shared activities, and mutual support in building and maintaining strong family bonds. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics.

Objective: To help students use target vocabulary related to family members and their routines while improving writing and speaking skills. Objective: To identify and talk about family members and their routines in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Choose the Correct Word
The teacher provides a worksheet with pictures depicting family-related activities and members (e.g., siblings playing, grandparents gardening, a mother cooking) along with a word bank containing words like siblings, grandparents, mother, gardening, cooking, relaxing, drawing, and painting. Students examine the pictures and write the correct word under each image (e.g., for grandparents gardening, write ''grandparents gardening''). Once completed, the teacher points to each picture, asks, ''Who is this, and what are they doing?'' and encourages students to respond in full sentences, such as ''These are grandparents, and they are gardening'', while providing feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To help students describe and compare family members’ routines and hobbies using visuals and target vocabulary.
Activity 2: Fill in the Blanks (Interactive with Visuals)
The teacher presents an interactive activity with pictures of family members performing tasks (e.g., cooking, gardening, teaching). Each question shows a visual with an incomplete sentence and multiplechoice options for students to select the correct word. For example, a picture of a mother cooking is paired with the sentence, ''My mother is a cook. She ____________ delicious meals every day'', with choices like ''cooks, teaches, and grows''. For comparisons, side-by-side visuals, such as a father farming and a mother teaching, are provided with sentences like ''My father ____________ vegetables, but my mother ____________ lessons'', followed by a comparative statement: ''My father’s job is ____________, but my mother’s job is ____________,'',with options like ''harder/easier'' or ''more rewarding/less tiring''. After completing the activity, students share their answers orally, forming sentences such as ''My father’s job is harder than my mother’s job, but my mother’s job is more rewarding than my father’s job''. The teacher provides feedback on grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation, reinforcing the use of comparative adjectives and target verbs. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Can: (My grandmother can cook amazing meals.)
-The Simple Present Tense: (We have dinner together every evening.)
-The Present Progressive Tense: (My brother is watching TV in the living room.)
-Question Tags (Simple Present and Present Progressive): (They go to the beach every Sunday, don’t they?)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'': The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Simple Future Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (I think my aunt will visit us tomorrow. I think my aunt won’t / will not visit me tomorrow. Will your aunt visit you tomorrow?)
-The Simple Present Tense for the Future (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (Our family meeting starts at 7 p.m. every Sunday. Our family meeting doesn’t / does not start at 7 p.m. every Saturday. Does your family meeting start at 7 p.m. every Sunday?)
-Be Going to Future Tense (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (We’re / are going to visit my grandparents next weekend. We’re not / are not going to visit my grandparents next weekend. Are you going to visit your grandparents next weekend?)
-The Present Progressive Tense for the Future (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (We’re / are having a family dinner on Friday night. We’re not / are not having a family dinner on Friday night. Are you having a family dinner on Friday night?)
Functions of the Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of ''Can'': Describing ability
-Use of the Simple Present Tense: Describing daily routines, job routines, work tasks, and hobbies of family members.
-Use of the Present Progressive Tense: Describing what family members are doing at home and at work now.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Future Tense: Making predictions, expressing plans or intention, asking about future actions.
-Use of the Simple Present Tense for the Future: Talking about scheduled or timetabled events in the future.
-Use of ''Be Going to Future'' Tense: Describing planned actions or making predictions based on evidence.
-Use of the Present Progressive Tense for the Future: Describing arranged future activities and routines.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
My Granddad is the heart of the family.
We always catch up with our relatives during the holidays!
My sister is into music. I’m super close to my mum/dad/sister/brother etc.
My mum is a bookworm.
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: f: (/f/); g: (/g/, /dʒ/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar:
Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family'' means, but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.
Key Concepts
Family members, routines, routines of family members, hobbies, hobbies of family members, relationships, relationships in the family.

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 5: Lıfe In The Neıghbourhood And Cıty
uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''life in the neighbourhood and city'', and covers the sub-themes of ''attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will create a comprehensive project about the attractions, recreational places, services, and transport in their neighbourhood and city. The project will include identifying key attractions such as parks, historical sites, museums, or shopping areas, and describing how these places contribute to the lifestyle of the community. Additionally, students will explore the essential services in their area, such as schools, hospitals, libraries, and community centres, and explain their significance in meeting the needs of residents. Transportation will also be a focus, with students checking the available options, including public transport, walking and cycling routes, and road networks, and discussing simply and talking about them. Students will design a visual presentation to accompany their project, such as a map or infographic, highlighting the locations of attractions, services, and transportation routes. They are encouraged to add photos, drawings, or symbols to make their work more engaging. Alongside the visual component, students will simply write a reflection on how these aspects contribute to making their neighbourhood and city liveable, discussing any challenges they observe, such as traffic or limited services, and proposing solutions for improvement. Finally, students will present their projects to the class, using their visuals to support a clear and engaging explanation. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics and a marking scheme.
uniteler.destekleme:
Objective: To identify and talk about neighbourhood attractions in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Neighbourhood Attractions and Adjectives Matching Game
The teacher provides students with two sets of cards: one with pictures or names of attractions (e.g., a park, a castle, a square) and another with adjectives (e.g., relaxing, historical, amazing). Students work in pairs to match the attractions with suitable adjectives (e.g., a park—relaxing, a castle—historical). After completing the matches, the teacher points to a card and asks simple questions like ''What is this?'' or ''How is it?'' Students respond with short answers, such as ''It’s a park'' or ''It’s relaxing.'' The pair with the most correct matches and answers wins the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about attractions, services, and transportation in the neighbourhood and city in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 2: Vocabulary Sorting Game
The teacher gives students a list of mixed words, such as a castle, a fire department, and a ferry, related to attractions, services, and transportation. Students work in pairs to sort the words into three categories: Attractions, Services, and Transportation. After sorting, the teacher points to a word and asks questions such as, ''What is this?'' or ''Where can you find it?''. Students answer with simple phrases, such as ''It’s a castle'' or ''In the city.'' Then the teacher asks other students to say the words in full sentences. After each answer, the teacher provides feedback, correcting any mistakes and praising accurate responses. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

uniteler.İçerik Çerçevesi:
LIFE IN THE NEIGHBOURHOOD AND CITY
Sub-themes: ''Attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary):
Vocabulary for attractions in the neighbourhood and city: Nouns: A bridge, a castle, a gallery, a hill, a monument, a square, a shop (store-AmE), a tower, an ancient/ historical site, an exhibition, an ancient/historical site, a natural site, a shore, a protected area. Adjectives: Foreign, amazing, exciting, local, relaxing, affordable, geological. Verbs: To discover, to explore, to relax. Vocabulary for services in the neighbourhood and city:
Nouns: A car park (parking lot-AmE), a delivery service, a shopping centre (department store) (a shopping mall-AmE), a fire station (fire department-AmE), a government office, a launderette (laundry-AmE), a water supply, a bakery, a crafts shop (craft store-AmE), a government office, a campsite, an advertisement (commercial-AmE), a crime, an event, rubbish (garbage/trash-AmE), safety, a pedestrian crossing/a zebra crossing) crosswalk-AmE), the Tube (London Underground) underground (subway-AmE), a ship, a harbour, a pedestrian, a roundabout, a square. Verbs: To access, to book, to deliver, to collect, to cost, to share.
Adjectives: Available, limited, noisy.
Vocabulary for transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Nouns: An accident, a boat, a bus, a ferry. Prepositional phrases for transportation: On foot, by train/metro.
Verbs: To cross, to pass, to return. Adjectives: Comfortable, crowded.
Vocabulary for locations and directions: Prepositions: Behind, beside, near, next to, between, across, through, along, around, centre, inside, outside, narrow, close, far.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:
29 October Republic Day'', ''23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day'', ''19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day'', ''15 July Democracy and National Unity Day'', ''30 August Victory Day'', ''Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)'', ''Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)''.
*(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Wh- questions: ''why, where'': (Where did you go last weekend?)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'':
The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
- The Simple Past Tense with Verb ''To be (was/were) (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (She was at school yesterday. She wasn’t at school yesterday. Was she at school yesterday?) (They were at school last Monday. They weren’t / were not at school last Monday. Were they at school last Monday?)
-The Simple Past Tense with Regular and Irregular Verbs (Affirmative, Negative, and Interrogative): (I met my old friend at school yesterday. I didn’t / did not meet my friends at school yesterday. Did you meet your friends at school yesterday?) (We played football at school yesterday. We didn’t / did not play football at school yesterday.)
-Comparative Adjectives: (The park is quieter than the main square. The museum is more interesting than the shopping centre.) -Conjunction ''When'': (I met with my best friend when I was at school.)
-Question Tags with the Simple Past Tense'': (Did you, didn’t you, were you, weren’t you, was she, wasn’t she) (They didn’t leave early, did they?)
-Gerunds and Infinitives'' ''-ing, to verb'': (She plans to go shopping.) (I like going shopping with my friends.)
-Prepositions of Place and Time: behind, among, beside, near, next to, between, across, into, through, onto, along, around, back, centre, inside, outside, wide, narrow, far, close.
-Prepositional phrases such as ''on foot'' etc.
Functions of the Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of -Wh- questions: ''why, where'': Asking for reasons, places, or further information.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Simple Past Tense with – to be (was/were): Describing where someone was or how someone felt in the past (past states).
-Use of the Simple Past Tense with Regular and Irregular Verbs: Talking about actions or events that happened and finished in the past.
-Use of Comparative Adjectives: Comparing differences between two people, places, things, or ideas and showing how one thing differs from another in terms of a quality or characteristic.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
We’re on the go!
Mind the gap!
A smooth ride!
We’re in good hands!
It’s a stone’s throw away!
Let’s hit the town!
That’s just around the corner!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Intonation of question tags (past).
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city'' means, but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.

Attractions in the neighbourhood, attractions in the city, recreational places in the neighbourhood, recreational places in the city, attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city, services in the neighbourhood, services in the city, services in the neighbourhood and city, transportation in the neighbourhood, transportation in the city, transportation in the neighbourhood and city.

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 6: Lıfe In The World
uniteler.aciklama: This theme is centred on the concept of ''life in the world'', and covers the subthemes of ''continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative, and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project about a simple global culinary adventure. In this project, they will pile up a booklet about culinary adventures to explore continents, countries, and food cultures of various regions. They will describe personal food preferences and shopping experiences for specific dietary needs (e.g., vegetarian, gluten-free). Students will create roles based on different countries and act out a shopping experience where they learn about and purchase traditional food from various cultures around the world. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics.

Objective: To help students differentiate between countable and uncountable nouns by using target vocabulary in English with visual aids and written activities.
Activity 1: Countable vs. Uncountable Nouns with Visuals
The teacher provides students with two sheets of paper. The first sheet contains only pictures of various foods and drinks (e.g., mushrooms, rice, milk). The second sheet is divided into two columns labelled ''Countable Nouns'' and ''Uncountable Nouns'', with a word bank at the top listing the names of the items shown in the pictures. Students first cut out the pictures from the first sheet, then sort and glue them into the correct column on the second sheet. Then, they refer to the word bank to write the appropriate name next to each glued picture (e.g., a picture of mushrooms is glued under ''Countable Nouns'' and ''mushroom'' is written beside it). Students share their completed work for teacher and peer feedback. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Verbs: To be surrounded.

Countries: Türkiye, United Kingdom-UK (England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, Wales), Great Briain-GB (informal) (England, Scotland, Wales), Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic/Czechia, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Bulgaria, Hungary, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, China, Japan, Russia, India, the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.

Vocabulary for food types:

Vocabulary for people according to food preferences:

Vocabulary for places, items, and people about food:

*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations:
29 October Republic Day'', ''23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day'', ''19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day'', ''15 July Democracy and National Unity Day'', ''30 August Victory Day'', ''Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)'', ''Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)''. *(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Curriculum.
Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Comparative Adjectives: (This curry is spicier than the one last week.)
*About ''Background Grammatical Structures in Use'':
The ''Background Grammatical Structures'' in this section are not only revisional but also serve as contextual support and contribute to meaning-making. They are intended to be used within the theme to help students grasp the meaning of the language constructed through the use of ''Target Grammatical Structures'' without being explicitly taught. These structures are not considered ''Target Grammatical Structures'' themselves rather they function as a part of the facilitation process, supporting both the target forms and the contexts in which they are used. They provide opportunities for learning through revised and scaffolded language.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-The Present Perfect Tense: (Positive, Negative, and Interrogative Forms): (They’ve / have eaten all the food since yesterday evening. They haven’t / have not eaten all the food yesterday. (Have they eaten all the food yesterday?)
-Question Tags with the Present Perfect Tense: (You have finished your food, haven’t you?
(With How Long? Since, For, Already, Just, Ever, Never):
How Long?: (How long have you shopped for traditional dishes?)
Since: (She has lived in Italy since 2020 and she loves Italian pasta.)
For: (I have been a vegetarian for three years.)
Already: (They have already tried kebab in Türkiye.)
Just: (We have just bought some fresh vegetables from the supermarket.)
Ever: (Have you ever tasted falafel from the Middle East?)
Never: (I have never eaten spicy Japanese food before.)
-Superlative Adjectives (Regular and irregular adjectives)
Regular: (Italy has the most delicious pasta dishes in the world.)
Irregular: (This is the best croissant I’ve ever eaten!)
-Countable and Uncountable Nouns:
Countable nouns (for food): (There are many baklavas in the shop window.)
Uncountable nouns (for food): (There is some rice in the pot.)
-Quantifiers: Some, any, much, many, a lot of, none, no, few, a few, little, a little
Little: (There is little rice left in the bag; we need to buy more.)
A Little: (I added a little garlic to the soup for extra flavour.)
Functions of the Background Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of Comparative Adjectives: Comparing differences between two people, places, things, or ideas and showing how one thing differs from another in terms of a quality or characteristic. Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use:
-Use of the Present Perfect Tense (With How Long? Since, For, Already, Just, Ever, Never): Describing actions or events that have a connection to the present; expressing duration, completion, or experience.
-Use of ''Question Tags'' with the Present Perfect Tense: Confirming information or seeking agreement about actions or events that have a connection to the present. -Use of Superlative Adjectives (Regular and Irregular Adjectives): Comparing more than two items or people to highlight the highest degree of a quality.
-Use of Countable and Uncountable Nouns: Differentiating between items that can be individually counted and those that cannot; describing quantities and making appropriate agreements with verbs and quantifiers.
-Use of Quantifiers: Some, any, much, many, a lot of, none, no, few, a few, little, a little: Describing and specifying amounts or quantities of countable and uncountable nouns in various contexts.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use:
The four corners of the world!
East meets West!
Shop till you drop!
You are what you eat!
We’re cooking up a storm!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use:
Consonants: j, k j:
(/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/), silent /k/)
*(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)
uniteler.Anahtar Kavramlar:
Generalisations
The target concept of this theme ''continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world'' is present in almost all languages. Students who start to learn a new language inevitably bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning context. For example, a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what ''continents, countries and nationalities, shopping for personal food preference, food and food culture from different parts of the world'' means, but may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language will help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information more easily in a foreign language, in this case English.
Key Concepts
Continents, countries, nationalities, shopping, personal food preference, shopping for personal food preference, food, food culture, food from different parts of the world, food culture from different parts of the world.

uniteler.baslik: Upper Secondary-Prep Year-Level: A2 - Theme 7: Lıfe In Nature
uniteler.aciklama:
This theme is centred on the concept of ''life in nature'', and covers the subthemes
of ''daily activities in nature, extreme weather conditions and adventures
in nature''. These components (sub-themes) are integrated into the learning
process through the contextualised use of target vocabulary, grammatical
structures, phonological features, and social language expressions. The
teaching and learning activities are designed to be meaningful, collaborative,
and communicative, and are tailored to align with the learners’ developmental
level, interests, needs, and preferences. The ultimate aim of this theme is to
equip learners with the knowledge, skills, and experiences needed to effectively
use English in their daily lives, both within and beyond the school environment.
uniteler.olcme: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project based on their experiences and imagination of daily activities in nature, extreme weather conditions, and adventures in nature. They will describe the roles people play in different outdoor activities, how weather conditions influence those activities, and the necessary preparations for adventures in nature. Students will write scripts for each role and act out different scenarios involving nature-based activities like hiking, camping, or experiencing extreme weather conditions. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics.

Objective: To describe what people were doing in nature in the past in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar.
Activity 1: Picture Story
The teacher tells the students that they do an activity where they describe what people were doing in nature in the past. The teacher provides a set of pictures depicting scenes such as someone hiking, a bird flying, or a child planting a tree. Students work in pairs to write sentences describing what was happening in each picture, such as ''She was planting a tree in the garden'', or ''The bird was flying over the lake''. After completing their sentences, students take turns reading them aloud to the class while focusing on clear pronunciation. The teacher provides constructive feedback on their grammar and pronunciation to help them improve. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
